# CPR-registeret

CPR-registeret (the Danish Civil Registration System) is the national register used to establish vital status — whether a patient is alive or dead — for patients included in [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]], the Danish national quality database for atrial fibrillation care. In the reporting used by [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]], mortality figures for atrial fibrillation patients are calculated by linking patient records to CPR-registeret to determine which patients have died and which remain alive [^src1] [^src2].

This linkage underpins the mortality quality indicator reported both in the 2023 report, covering the period 1 July 2022 to 30 June 2023, and in the 2024 report, which shows mortality among atrial fibrillation patients declining since 2021/2022. In this broader reporting, CPR-registeret is used alongside the Landspatientregisteret (National Patient Registry) as a core data source, feeding national and regional mortality statistics, incidence data, and demographic characteristics for both prevalent and newly diagnosed patients across Denmark's five regions [^src2].

CPR-registeret itself does not appear in the corpus with further institutional detail beyond its role as the data source for vital status; its documented significance in this wiki is specifically its function of supplying death/alive status data used in the mortality analyses of the atrial fibrillation database [^src1] [^src2].
